adjudication_note: Joint evidence supports TREES thermoacoustic energy generation/distribution and recycling waste heat by transporting thermal energy to end users.

Evidence supports fuel-ignition, battery-pack, and hybrid-safety concerns, but the claim incorrectly folds the fossil-fuel/fire assumption of an existing regulation into hazards introduced by the hybrid power system.
Joint evidence supports fuel-system ignition concerns, battery-pack hazards, and operational constraints/safety considerations during demonstrator testing.
Evidence directly supports ambient-air forced convection and CHT analysis/optimization of aerodynamic and heat-transfer performance.
Evidence directly states that EAP heat comes from motor windings, power electronics, batteries, and other components not intrinsically coupled to freestream like a turbine engine.
Evidence directly supports NDE detection of defect precursors and an ultrasonic frequency-domain method sensitive to embedded battery defects.
Evidence says batteries will likely be located in unpressurized compartments without conditioned air; the claim turns that likely design assumption into a definite location.
Evidence directly states this as a potential solution for reducing heat-rejection requirements during takeoff and initial climb.
Evidence directly lists cryo-fuel storage/handling, thermal management, combustion, scalable engines/fuel cells, and architecture/system integration as challenges.
Evidence supports improvements in cost, safety, reliability, noise, and efficiency, but the cited chunk does not fully establish the broader environmental-impact claim.

Evidence supports system-weight comparison, high conversion efficiency, and improving battery energy density, but does not support the claimed higher-voltage-at-altitude characteristic and overstates some items as defining capabilities.
Evidence directly states the EAP definition, new degradation/fault health-management challenges, required electrical/control knowledge, and current/voltage sensing.
Evidence directly links high electricity-to-shaft conversion efficiency to reduced total energy use and dramatic emissions reductions.
Evidence directly states that heating/ignition of one battery cell can cascade to neighboring cells.
The cited chunk describes TMS scope and design variables but does not contain the claimed motor-winding/power-electronics/battery loss mechanism or jet-exhaust heat-rejection comparison.
